confusions: The Who pays page had lots of big numbers and I could not find the tax-type breakdown for the lowest fifth there; I had to go to Tax and income.
Class sizes for a chosen year were buried in a collapsed 'More on' box after using the year picker, and cost me many taps.
The year-compare page listed holidays and work but not class sizes in the main list, so I scrolled up and down a lot.
Holiday figures changed from UK to Great Britain residents and a new method, which made 2015 vs 2025 confusing; I did not find a direct comparison.
Several pages say 'fifth', 'gross household income' and 'tax year', which I had to guess at.
The spending page gives only pounds per £100 for each area, so I had to compare bars to see defence was smaller than health.
I could not find a legal class-size limit stated, only a 'classes of more than 30' link, so I guessed 30.
Most visited country was hidden inside a collapsed table I nearly missed.
The household tax page has several similar percentages (33.6%, 36.2%, 46.0%) and I had to read carefully to tell them apart.
Nothing on the pages I opened said how to show a missing year or a break in a chart, so I picked the sensible-sounding answer.
The page only scrolls a little at a time, so I skipped bits of text and could not find some answers.
I could not tell which menu page would have immigration, defence, manifesto or the other topics, so I gave up on them.
The top-1% page only showed one year, so I could not tell whether it was the same in every year.
Debt page gave two different debt measures (IMF and OECD) and I was not sure which one to trust.
